sections.heading: Accepted payment methods
sections.text: Workspaces can pay by credit or debit card on any paid plan. Yearly plans with a total of 2,000 USD or more can also pay by bank transfer against an invoice, with payment due within 30 days. Prices are charged in USD, EUR or GBP; the currency is chosen when the first paid plan starts and can only be changed by support.

sections.heading: Billing invoices
sections.text: Pellbrook sends a billing invoice to the billing email address after every payment. Owners can download all past billing invoices as PDF files from Settings, then Billing, then Invoice history. These are invoices for your subscription, not the invoices you send to your own clients.

sections.heading: Sales tax and VAT
sections.text: Customers in the European Union are charged VAT at their country's rate unless they enter a valid VAT ID in the billing settings. Customers in the United Kingdom are charged UK VAT. A VAT ID added later applies from the next invoice; past invoices are not reissued.

sections.heading: Changing the billing email
sections.text: Only the workspace owner can change the billing email address and the payment card.

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.text: An upgrade starts at once. You pay the price difference for the rest of the current billing period, prorated by day. New features are available as soon as the payment goes through.

sections.heading: Downgrading
sections.text: A downgrade takes effect at the end of the current billing period, monthly or yearly. Until then you keep the features of your current plan. Before the downgrade, check that the lower plan supports your number of users and projects; extra projects are archived, not deleted.

sections.heading: Cancelling a subscription
sections.text: Cancelling stops the next renewal. The workspace keeps its paid plan until the end of the period that was already paid for, and then moves to the Free plan. Cancelling a subscription does not delete your data. To delete the workspace and all its data, see Closing your account.

title: Adding and removing users on a paid plan

sections.heading: Adding users
sections.text: When you invite a new user to a paid workspace, you pay for the rest of the current billing period straight away. The charge is prorated by day. For example, adding one Team user halfway through a monthly period costs about half of one month's price.

sections.heading: Removing users on monthly billing
sections.text: When you remove a user on a monthly plan, the unused days become a credit. The credit is applied to your next invoice automatically. Credits are not paid out as cash.

sections.heading: Removing users on yearly billing
sections.text: On yearly billing, removing a user frees the seat for someone else, but the number of paid seats only goes down at the next renewal. To lower the seat count at renewal, change the seat number in Settings, then Billing before the renewal date.

sections.heading: Deactivated users
sections.text: Deactivated users are not counted as paid users. Their past time entries stay in reports and invoices.

sections.heading: Common error codes
sections.text: Status 401 means the token is missing, wrong or revoked. Status 403 means the token is valid but the user may not do this action, for example a member trying to edit another member's entries, or a write call on the Starter plan. Status 404 means the item does not exist or the user cannot see it. Status 422 means a field is missing or has a wrong value; the response lists the fields.

sections.heading: Revoked tokens
sections.text: A token stops working when the user revokes it, when the user is deactivated or when the user changes their password. Create a new token after a password change.

sections.heading: Time formats
sections.text: All times in the API are in UTC and use the ISO 8601 format. Durations are given in seconds.

sections.heading: Access and tokens
sections.text: The Pellbrook Hours API is a REST API that returns JSON. Each user creates a personal API token in Profile, then API tokens. A token has the same permissions as the user who created it. Starter plans have read-only access; Team and Business plans can read and write.

sections.heading: Rate limits
sections.text: Requests are limited per workspace: 60 requests per minute on Starter, 120 per minute on Team and 600 per minute on Business. When you go over the limit, the API answers with status 429 and a Retry-After header that says how many seconds to wait.

sections.heading: Pagination
sections.text: List endpoints return up to 100 items per page. Use the cursor value from the response to ask for the next page. Results are sorted by the time they were last changed.

title: Client did not receive an invoice email

sections.heading: Check the address and the spam folder
sections.text: Open the invoice and check the client's email address. Ask the client to look in their spam or junk folder. Invoice emails are sent from invoices@pellbrook.example with your company name as the sender name.

sections.heading: Bounced addresses
sections.text: If an email address bounced before, we stop sending to it. The invoice then shows the status Not delivered. Correct the address on the client record and send the invoice again.

sections.heading: Sending the PDF yourself
sections.text: You can always download the invoice as a PDF and send it from your own email.

sections.heading: Rounding
sections.text: If a project uses rounding, report totals use rounded time, while the timesheet shows exact time. Each entry is rounded on its own, so totals can differ by several minutes. Switch rounding off in the report options to compare exact times.

sections.heading: Time zones
sections.text: Reports use the time zone of the person viewing them. An entry made late at night can fall on a different day for a colleague in another time zone, which changes daily and weekly totals.

sections.heading: Filters
sections.text: Check the approval and billable filters. A report filtered to approved time leaves out timesheets that are still waiting for approval.

sections.heading: Forgotten password
sections.text: Choose Forgot password on the sign-in page and enter your email address. The reset link is valid for one hour and can be used once. If the email does not arrive within a few minutes, check your spam folder.

sections.heading: Lost the phone with your two-step codes
sections.text: Use one of the 10 recovery codes you saved when you turned on two-step sign-in. Each code works once. If you have no recovery codes left, ask a workspace admin to reset two-step sign-in for your account; owners must contact support and prove their identity.

sections.heading: Single sign-on users
sections.text: If your workspace requires single sign-on, the password form does not work for you. Choose Sign in with SSO and enter your work email address.

sections.heading: Too many attempts
sections.text: After 10 failed sign-in attempts in 15 minutes, sign-in for that account is paused for 15 minutes.

sections.heading: Check the offline banner
sections.text: If the orange offline banner is showing, the phone has no connection to Pellbrook Hours. Entries are kept on the phone for up to 7 days and will sync when the connection is back. Pull down on the Timesheet screen to try again.

sections.heading: Turn off battery optimisation
sections.text: Some Android phones stop apps from working in the background to save battery. Open the Android Settings, then Apps, then Pellbrook Hours, then Battery, and choose Unrestricted. Without this, entries may only sync while the app is open.

sections.heading: Do not clear the app storage
sections.text: Clearing the app storage or signing out deletes entries that have not synced yet. Let the waiting entries sync first.

sections.heading: Check the offline banner
sections.text: If the orange offline banner is showing, the phone has no connection to Pellbrook Hours. Entries are kept on the phone for up to 7 days and will sync when the connection is back. Pull down on the Timesheet screen to try again.

sections.heading: Allow background refresh
sections.text: On iPhone, entries only sync in the background if Background App Refresh is on for Pellbrook Hours. Open the iPhone Settings, then General, then Background App Refresh, and switch it on for the app. Low Power Mode also pauses background refresh.

sections.heading: Do not sign out with waiting entries
sections.text: Signing out of the app deletes entries that have not synced yet. If the banner shows entries waiting to sync, connect to the internet and let them sync before you sign out or delete the app.

sections.heading: The timer stopped by itself
sections.text: A timer stops automatically after 24 hours. It also stops when you start another timer on any device, because each user can run only one timer at a time.

sections.heading: The timer shows on one device but not another
sections.text: The running timer is shared across the web, desktop and mobile apps. If a device shows an old state, refresh the web page or pull down on the mobile Timesheet screen. A phone that is offline shows the timer it knew about when it lost the connection.

sections.heading: Idle time was not detected
sections.text: Idle detection works only in the desktop app. On macOS, the app needs the Accessibility permission in System Settings, then Privacy and Security, to notice keyboard and mouse activity.

sections.heading: How approvals work
sections.text: On the Team and Business plans, admins can turn on approvals in Settings, then Approvals. Members then submit their timesheet once a week. Their manager reviews it and approves it or sends it back with a comment.

sections.heading: Who approves
sections.text: Each member has one approver, which is their manager by default. Admins can choose a different approver for any member. If the approver is away, any admin can approve the timesheet.

sections.heading: Locked timesheets
sections.text: An approved timesheet is locked, and its entries cannot be changed or deleted. To change a locked entry, an admin reopens the timesheet, which sends it back to the member. Admins can also lock all timesheets older than a set number of days, even if they were not approved, with the Auto-lock setting.

sections.heading: Setting a budget
sections.text: On the Team and Business plans, each project can have a budget in hours or in money. Open the project, then Budget, and enter the amount. A budget can be a total for the whole project or reset every month.

sections.heading: Budget alerts
sections.text: Pellbrook Hours sends an email alert to the project managers when a project reaches 80% of its budget and again when it reaches 100%. Since version 5.3 you can add your own alert levels, for example 50% or 90%. Members do not get budget emails unless a manager adds them to the alert list.

sections.heading: Going over budget
sections.text: Time can still be tracked after a budget is used up. The project bar turns red on the dashboard, and the over-budget amount is shown in the project report.

sections.heading: Supported systems
sections.text: The desktop app runs on Windows 10 or newer and on macOS 12 or newer. It shows the running timer in the system tray on Windows and in the menu bar on macOS.

sections.heading: Keyboard shortcut
sections.text: Press Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows or Cmd+Shift+Space on macOS to start or stop the timer from any app. The shortcut can be changed in the desktop app settings.

sections.heading: Updates
sections.text: The desktop app checks for updates when it starts and installs them the next time you open it. Your administrator can turn off automatic updates with the managed install package.

sections.heading: Report exports
sections.text: Any report can be exported as CSV, Excel or PDF from the Export button above the report. The export follows the filters and the rounding of the report you are looking at. CSV and Excel exports need the Starter plan or higher; PDF export of the Summary report is available on every plan.

sections.heading: Full data export
sections.text: Owners and admins can export everything in the workspace from Settings, then Data export. You get a ZIP file of CSV files with time entries, projects, clients, tasks, members and invoices. Large workspaces receive an email with a download link when the file is ready; the link works for 7 days.

sections.heading: Calendar import
sections.text: Connect a work calendar in Profile, then Calendar to see your meetings next to your timesheet. Click a meeting to turn it into a time entry. Calendar import is available on every plan.

sections.heading: Accounting integration
sections.text: On the Team and Business plans, sent invoices can be copied to your accounting system automatically, with the client, line items, taxes and payment status. Payments recorded in the accounting system are copied back to Pellbrook Hours once an hour.

sections.heading: Webhooks
sections.text: On the Team and Business plans, admins can add webhooks in Settings, then Webhooks. A webhook sends a message to your own address when a time entry, project or invoice is created, changed or deleted. Failed deliveries are retried 5 times over one hour.

sections.heading: Creating an invoice
sections.text: Choose Invoices, then New invoice, pick a client and a date range. Pellbrook Hours adds all billable, not yet invoiced time for that client, using the billable rates and the project rounding. You can add fixed items, such as expenses, and a discount.

sections.heading: Taxes, currency and numbering
sections.text: An invoice can carry up to two taxes, for example a sales tax and a second local tax. Each client has its own invoice currency. Invoice numbers go up by one automatically, and you can set the starting number and a prefix in Settings, then Invoicing.

sections.heading: Sending and tracking
sections.text: Send the invoice by email from the app or download it as a PDF. Each invoice shows its status: draft, sent, viewed, partly paid or paid. You record payments yourself; Pellbrook Hours does not collect money from your clients.

sections.heading: Invoice limits
sections.text: The Starter plan includes up to 20 invoices per month. Team and Business have no invoice limit. The Free plan has no invoicing.

sections.heading: Adding time by hand
sections.text: If you forgot to start a timer, add the time by hand. In the Timesheet view, click a day and enter a duration such as 1:30 or 1.5, or enter a start and end time. Manual entries are marked with a small pencil icon in reports so managers can tell them apart from timer entries.

sections.heading: Editing entries
sections.text: You can edit the project, task, note, date and duration of your own entries. Admins and managers can edit entries of the people on their projects. Entries that are part of an approved timesheet or a sent invoice are locked; see Timesheet approvals.

sections.heading: Bulk edit
sections.text: Select several entries in the Timesheet view to move them to another project, mark them billable or non-billable, or delete them together.

sections.heading: Supported phones
sections.text: The Pellbrook Hours mobile app runs on iPhone with iOS 16 or newer and on Android 10 or newer. It is free to download and works with every plan.

sections.heading: Offline mode
sections.text: The mobile app keeps working without a connection. Timers and new entries are saved on the phone for up to 7 days and sent to your workspace when the phone is back online. An orange banner at the top of the screen shows that you are offline and how many entries are waiting to sync.

sections.heading: What the mobile app cannot do
sections.text: Invoices, approvals and workspace settings are only available in the web app. The mobile app has no idle detection.

sections.heading: Projects and clients
sections.text: Every time entry belongs to a project. A project can be linked to a client, and a client can have many projects. Projects can be billable or non-billable, and you can add tasks to a project to split the work.

sections.heading: Which billable rate is used
sections.text: A billable rate can be set at four levels. Pellbrook Hours uses the most specific rate it finds, in this order: the task rate, then the member's rate on that project, then the project rate, then the workspace default rate. If none is set, the time is billable at zero.

sections.heading: Changing a rate
sections.text: When you change a rate, you choose whether it applies only to new time or also to past entries that are not yet invoiced. Entries on sent invoices keep the rate they were invoiced at.

sections.heading: Report types
sections.text: There are three reports. The Summary report groups time by project, client, member or task. The Detailed report lists every entry. The Weekly report shows hours per member per day.

sections.heading: Filters and saved reports
sections.text: Filter any report by date range, project, client, member, task, billable status and approval status. Save a filtered report to open it again later or to share it with a link. Shared report links can be opened without signing in and can be turned off at any time.

sections.heading: Scheduled reports
sections.text: On the Team and Business plans, a saved report can be emailed every day, week or month to up to 20 addresses. Scheduled reports were added in version 5.2.

sections.heading: Time zones in reports
sections.text: Reports use the time zone of the person viewing them. A shared or scheduled report uses the time zone of the person who saved it.

sections.heading: Standard roles
sections.text: There are four standard roles. The Owner controls billing and can do everything. Admins manage members, projects, rates and settings, but not billing. Managers see and edit time on the projects they manage and approve timesheets for their team. Members track their own time and see their own reports.

sections.heading: Seeing billable rates
sections.text: By default only owners and admins see billable rates and amounts. Admins can let managers see rates for their projects in Settings, then Permissions.

sections.heading: Custom roles
sections.text: On the Business plan, admins can create custom roles by starting from a standard role and switching single permissions on or off, for example letting a member create projects.

sections.heading: How rounding works
sections.text: Rounding is set per project under Project settings, then Rounding. You can round each entry up, down or to the nearest 6, 15 or 30 minutes. Rounding is off by default.

sections.heading: What rounding changes
sections.text: Rounding is applied in reports and on invoices. The original entries are never changed, so you can always switch rounding off and see the exact tracked time again. Because each entry is rounded on its own, the rounded total of a report can differ from the exact total.

sections.heading: Rounding and budgets
sections.text: Project budgets always use the exact tracked time, not the rounded time.

sections.heading: Starting and stopping a timer
sections.text: Press Start on the web app, the desktop app or the mobile app to begin tracking. Pick a project and, if you like, a task and a note. Press Stop when you finish; the time entry is saved straight away. Each user can have only one running timer. Starting a new timer stops the one that is running.

sections.heading: Timers that run too long
sections.text: A timer that runs for 24 hours stops by itself, and the entry is marked for review. You can edit the end time of any entry afterwards.

sections.heading: Idle detection
sections.text: The desktop app notices when you have not used the keyboard or mouse for 10 minutes while a timer is running. When you come back, it asks whether to keep the idle time, discard it or save it as a separate entry. The idle limit can be changed from 5 to 60 minutes in the desktop app settings. Idle detection is not available in the web app or the mobile app.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Pellbrook Hours has four plans: Free, Starter, Team and Business. Every paid plan is priced per user per month. A user is anyone who can sign in to the workspace, including admins. Guests who only receive shared reports are not counted as users.

sections.heading: Free plan
sections.text: The Free plan is for up to 3 users and 2 active projects. It includes timers, manual time entries and the summary report. Report history on the Free plan covers the last 30 days. Invoicing, approvals and integrations are not included.

sections.heading: Starter plan
sections.text: Starter costs 6 USD per user per month when billed monthly, or 5 USD per user per month when billed yearly. It adds unlimited projects, client records, CSV and Excel exports, one year of report history and invoicing for up to 20 invoices per month. Starter includes read-only access to the API.

sections.heading: Team plan
sections.text: Team costs 11 USD per user per month when billed monthly, or 9 USD per user per month when billed yearly. It adds timesheet approvals, project budgets with alerts, unlimited invoices, scheduled email reports, webhooks, the accounting integration and full access to the API. Report history is unlimited.

sections.heading: Business plan
sections.text: Business costs 19 USD per user per month when billed monthly, or 16 USD per user per month when billed yearly, with a minimum of 10 users. It adds single sign-on, custom roles, the audit log, a choice of data region, a 99.9% uptime commitment and priority support.

sections.heading: Free trial
sections.text: Every new workspace starts with a 14-day free trial of the Team plan. No payment card is needed to start the trial. When the trial ends, the workspace moves to the Free plan unless an owner chooses a paid plan. Data entered during the trial is kept, but features outside the Free plan are switched off and projects beyond the first 2 are archived, not deleted.

sections.heading: Extending a trial
sections.text: An owner can ask support for one trial extension of 7 days. Extensions are given once per workspace and only before the original trial ends.

sections.heading: Nonprofit discount
sections.text: Registered nonprofit organisations get 30% off any paid plan. To apply, the workspace owner sends proof of nonprofit status to support from the owner's email address. The discount starts from the next invoice and is reviewed every year.

sections.heading: Education discount
sections.text: Schools, universities and students get 50% off the Starter and Team plans. The education discount does not apply to the Business plan.

sections.heading: Discounts cannot be combined
sections.text: Only one discount can apply to a workspace at a time. Yearly billing already lowers the price, and it can be used together with one discount.

sections.heading: Workspace owner
sections.text: Each workspace has exactly one owner. The owner controls billing, can close the workspace and can transfer ownership. To transfer ownership, the owner opens Settings, then Members, picks an admin and chooses Make owner. The new owner must accept by email within 7 days.

sections.heading: If the owner has left the company
sections.text: If the owner can no longer be reached, an admin can ask support to transfer ownership. Support needs a written request from a company email address on the same domain as the workspace, and a confirmation from a second admin.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.text: Workspaces may not be used to track people without their knowledge. Pellbrook Hours records only the time that users enter or start themselves; it does not take screenshots, record keystrokes or track location.

sections.heading: Deleted time entries
sections.text: Deleted time entries move to the Trash, where they stay for 30 days. Any user can restore their own entries from the Trash during that time; admins can restore anyone's entries. After 30 days they are removed for good.

sections.heading: Archived and deleted projects
sections.text: Archived projects are kept with all their time entries for as long as the workspace exists, and they can be unarchived at any time. Deleted projects also go to the Trash for 30 days, together with their time entries, and are then removed for good.

sections.heading: Closing your account
sections.text: When an owner closes a workspace, all of its data is deleted 60 days after the closure. During those 60 days the owner can reopen the workspace by contacting support. Backup copies are removed within a further 35 days.

sections.heading: Exporting before you leave
sections.text: You can export all time entries, projects, clients and invoices at any time from Settings, then Data export, whatever plan you are on. The export is a ZIP file of CSV files.

sections.heading: Payment retries
sections.text: If a card payment fails, we retry it three times over 10 days and email the billing contact after each failed attempt. You can update the card at any time in Settings, then Billing; we then retry the payment within the hour.

sections.heading: Read-only mode
sections.text: If the payment is still not made 14 days after the first failure, the workspace becomes read-only. Users can sign in, view and export data, but cannot start timers or add, edit or invoice time.

sections.heading: Deletion of unpaid workspaces
sections.text: If a workspace stays unpaid for 90 days after the first failed payment, it is closed and its data is deleted. We email the owner 30 days and 7 days before this happens. Paying the overdue amount at any point before deletion restores full access at once.

sections.heading: Data processing agreement
sections.text: Pellbrook offers a data processing agreement for every paid plan. Owners can sign it online from Settings, then Privacy. The list of subprocessors is kept on the same page, and we email owners 30 days before adding a new subprocessor.

sections.heading: Data region
sections.text: Workspaces on the Business plan can choose to store their data in the EU region or the US region. All other plans store data in the US region. Moving an existing workspace to another region is done by support and takes the workspace offline for up to two hours during a planned window.

sections.heading: Personal data requests
sections.text: Users can download a copy of their own personal data from Profile, then Privacy. Requests to delete a person's data from a workspace are handled by the workspace owner, who is the data controller.

sections.heading: Monthly plans
sections.text: Monthly plans are not refunded. When you cancel or downgrade a monthly plan, you keep access until the end of the month you paid for, and no partial-month refund is given.

sections.heading: Yearly plans
sections.text: Yearly plans can be refunded in full within 30 days of the first purchase or of a renewal. After 30 days, the yearly fee is not refunded, but you can downgrade or cancel so that the plan does not renew.

sections.heading: How to ask for a refund
sections.text: The workspace owner asks for a refund by writing to support from the owner's email address. Refunds go back to the original payment method within 10 business days. Bank transfer payments are refunded by bank transfer.

sections.heading: Charges after a failed cancellation
sections.text: If you were charged after you tried to cancel and the cancellation did not go through because of an error on our side, we refund that charge in full, whatever the plan.

sections.heading: Encryption
sections.text: All data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or newer, and at rest with AES-256. Payment card details are never stored on Pellbrook servers; they are handled by our payment processor.

sections.heading: Two-step sign-in
sections.text: Any user can turn on two-step sign-in with an authenticator app in Profile, then Security. Owners and admins can require two-step sign-in for everyone in the workspace from Settings, then Security. Each user gets 10 one-time recovery codes when they turn it on.

sections.heading: Audits and reports
sections.text: Pellbrook is audited every year against SOC 2 Type II. Customers on the Business plan can ask for the latest report under a non-disclosure agreement.

sections.heading: Reporting a security issue
sections.text: If you think you have found a security issue, write to the security team at security@pellbrook.example. We reply within two business days.

sections.heading: Support channels
sections.text: All plans, including Free, can email support. Team and Business plans can also use live chat inside the app. Support hours are Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 20:00 UTC.

sections.heading: Response times
sections.text: We answer email within one business day on Free and Starter, and within 8 business hours on Team. Business plan requests get priority support with a first reply within 4 business hours.

sections.heading: Uptime commitment
sections.text: On the Business plan, Pellbrook commits to 99.9% uptime each calendar month. If uptime falls below 99.9%, the workspace gets a service credit of 10% of that month's fee; below 99.0%, the credit is 25%. Planned maintenance announced at least 48 hours ahead is not counted as downtime. Current status and past incidents are shown on the status page.

sections.heading: Longer offline mode
sections.text: The mobile app now keeps unsynced entries for up to 7 days without a connection. Before 5.1 the limit was 3 days.

sections.heading: Calendar import
sections.text: You can now connect a work calendar and turn meetings into time entries with one click.

sections.heading: Fixes
sections.text: Fixed a problem where the desktop app showed the wrong total after the computer woke from sleep.

sections.heading: Scheduled reports
sections.text: Saved reports can now be emailed every day, week or month on the Team and Business plans.

sections.heading: Auto-lock
sections.text: Admins can lock timesheets older than a set number of days, even if they were not approved.

sections.heading: API
sections.text: List endpoints now use a cursor for paging instead of page numbers. Page numbers still work until the end of 2026.

sections.heading: Custom budget alerts
sections.text: Besides the alerts at 80% and 100% of a budget, you can now add your own alert levels to any project budget.

sections.heading: Data region choice
sections.text: Business workspaces can now choose to keep their data in the EU region or the US region.

sections.heading: Keyboard shortcut on macOS
sections.text: The global timer shortcut now works on macOS as well as Windows. The default is Cmd+Shift+Space.

sections.heading: Create the workspace
sections.text: Sign up with your work email and name the workspace after your company. You become the workspace owner. Set the workspace time zone, the first day of the week and the default currency in Settings, then General.

sections.heading: Invite your team
sections.text: Open Settings, then Members and choose Invite. Enter email addresses one per line or upload a CSV file. Invitations expire after 7 days; you can resend an expired invitation from the same page. On a paid plan, each accepted invitation adds a paid user.

sections.heading: Set up projects and rates
sections.text: Create your clients and projects, add tasks if you need them and set the billable rates. If you already track time in spreadsheets, you can import it; see Importing time from a spreadsheet.

sections.heading: Preparing the file
sections.text: Save your spreadsheet as a CSV file. The required columns are Date, Member email, Project and Duration. Optional columns are Client, Task, Note, Billable and Start time. Dates must be in the YYYY-MM-DD format, and durations in hours and minutes such as 1:30 or in decimal hours such as 1.5.

sections.heading: Running the import
sections.text: Open Settings, then Import and upload the file. Each file can have up to 10,000 rows. Pellbrook Hours shows a preview with any problem rows before anything is saved. Projects and clients that do not exist yet are created for you; members must already be in the workspace.

sections.heading: Undoing an import
sections.text: An admin can undo a whole import within 24 hours from the import history on the same page.

sections.heading: Accept your invitation
sections.text: Open the invitation email and choose Join workspace. If your company uses single sign-on, you sign in with your company account and do not need a separate password.

sections.heading: Track your first hour
sections.text: Install the desktop or mobile app if you like, or use the web app. Press Start, pick a project and press Stop when you are done. Your entries appear in the Timesheet view, where you can fix anything you forgot.

sections.heading: Submit your week
sections.text: If your workspace uses approvals, press Submit week at the end of each week. You get an email if your manager sends the timesheet back.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.text: Single sign-on is available on the Business plan and works with any identity provider that supports SAML 2.0. You need to be the workspace owner or an admin, and you need to verify your company email domain first.

sections.heading: Turning it on
sections.text: In Settings, then Security, choose Single sign-on and copy the service details into your identity provider. Then paste the provider's sign-in address and certificate into Pellbrook Hours and press Test. We recommend testing with a second admin account before you make single sign-on required.

sections.heading: Required single sign-on
sections.text: When single sign-on is required, members can no longer sign in with a password. The workspace owner can always sign in with a password and a second step, so the workspace cannot be locked out if the identity provider is down.
